# Descriptive statistics

Table 1. Socio-demographic descriptive statistics.

```{r}
# table showing N and % by migration backgroundn, ECEC coverage (Low Medium High), Income (Low Medium High), Education Low Medium High, Age (4 cat), Parity (First brn vs subsequent), HH structure, working full time


CompareSamples <-MainDB %>%
  mutate(
    Control = ifelse(Assignment == "Control", 1, 0),
    SingleMum1or0 = ifelse(SingleMum == TRUE, 1, 0),
    Active1or0 = ifelse(Act3 == "Active", 1, 0),
    Educ1or0  = ifelse(Educ == "Sup", 1, 0),
    BornFr1or0  = ifelse(FrenchYNBaseline == "France", 1, 0),
    EverUsedECS1or0  = ifelse(UsedECEC == "Oui", 1, 0),
    PlanToUseECS1or0 = ifelse(ECSPlanToBaseline == TRUE, 1, 0),
    ComputerYes1or0 = ifelse(ComputerYN == "Oui", 1, 0),
    HighECSCov1or0 = ifelse(HighLowECECBaseline == "High ECEC covering", 1, 0), 
    DepParis1or0  = ifelse(Dep == "75", 1, 0),
    KnowsCrecheOnly1or0  = ifelse(KnowsCrecheOnly == TRUE, 1, 0),
    Primipare1or0 = ifelse(Primipare == TRUE, 1, 0), 
    WorkPlanTo1or0 = ifelse(WorkPlanTo == TRUE, 1, 0), 
    DeprivHolidays1or0 = ifelse(DeprivHolidays != "Pas du tout", 1, 0), NumberChildren = as.numeric(NumberChildren), 
    BabyFemale = ifelse(BabyFemale == TRUE, 1, 0)
  ) %>%
  select(Educ2,
    "Single parent family" = SingleMum1or0,
    #  "Couple cohabiting" = CoupleCohabiting1or0,
    "Age of the mother" = Age,
    "Number of children" = NumberChildren,
    "Parity (first born vs subsequent)" = Primipare1or0,
    "Mother is born in France" = BornFr1or0,

    #  "The mothers is not born in MENAnorAsia" = BirthNotAsiaMENA1or0,
    "The mother is active at baseline" = Active1or0,
    "Household earns less than €2,500 per month" = FmilyEarnLessThan2500,
    #  "The family couldn't afford holidays" = DeprivHolidays1or0,
    #  "Has a computer" = ComputerYes1or0,
    "Mother is present oriented" = Discount501or0,
    "Mother wants to work after maternity leaves" = WorkPlanTo1or0,
    #"The mother did not smoke" = DidNotSmoke1or0,
    #"The mother wants to breastfeed" = BreastFeedIntend1or0, 
    "Household has ever used early childcare" = EverUsedECS1or0,                  # Used: yes/no/ don't wanna answer
    "Mother wants to use early childcare" = PlanToUseECS1or0,                 # Intend to use, block variable
    #  "Knows early childcare is subsidised" = AffordSubsidies1or0,
    #  "Knows only daycare" = KnowsCrecheOnly1or0,
    #    "Value socialization" = ValSocialisation,
    #"Believe in returns to early childcare" = LikertReturnHK1or0,
    #"The mother trusts early childcare" = TrustCreche1or0,
    "Mother lives in Paris" = DepParis1or0,
    "Early childcare coverage is high" = HighECSCov1or0,
    "Child is a girl" = BabyFemale
  )


# Create balance table using tbl_summary
summary_baseline_variables_endline <- CompareSamples %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = Educ2,  # Comparison by baseline and endline
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{p}% ({n})"
    ),
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 2,
    missing = "no"
  ) %>%
  add_overall() %>%
  add_p(pvalue_fun = ~ style_pvalue(.x, digits = 3)) %>% 
  add_q(method = "fdr", pvalue_fun = ~ style_pvalue(.x, digits = 3)) %>% 
  add_significance_stars(thresholds = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1)) %>%
  modify_header(label ~ "**Variable**", stat_0 ~ "Overall", stat_1 ~ "High-SES", stat_2 ~ "Low-SES") %>%
  modify_spanning_header(c("stat_1", "stat_2") ~ "**Sample**")

# Convert to a flextable for formatting
summary_baseline_variables_endline %>%
  as_flex_table() %>%
  merge_v(part = "header", j = 1) %>%
  merge_h(part = "header", i = 1) %>%
  italic(j = 1, part = "body") |>  
  width(j = c(1), unit = "cm", width = 3) |>
  width(j = c(2:5), unit = "cm", width = 2) |>
  set_caption(caption = "Distribution of characteristics across high- and low-SES samples") %>%
  add_footer_lines(
    "Proportions and number of observations in parentheses for categorical and dichotomous variables. 
    Averages and standard deviations in parentheses for continuous variables. 
    Q-value control for the false discovery rate using FDR correction."
  ) %>%
  fontsize(i = 1, size = 10, part = "footer")


```

Alluvial plot on all

```{r}


library(ggalluvial)


# Ensure your data is in the correct format for ggalluvial
alluvial_data <- MainDB %>%
  dplyr::select(ChildcareTypeEndline, ChildcareTypeBaseline, Assignment) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ChildcareTypeBaseline) & !is.na(ChildcareTypeEndline))

# Create the alluvial plot
ggplot(alluvial_data,
       aes(axis1 = ChildcareTypeBaseline, axis2 = ChildcareTypeEndline)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = ChildcareTypeBaseline), width = 1/12) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/12, fill = "gray") +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 3) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Desired Care (During Pregnancy)", "Actual Care (Endline)"),
                   expand = c(0.15, 0.15)) +
  theme_minimal() 
```

# The social stratification of intention, application and access

```{r}
library(fixest)
library(modelsummary)
cm <- c( '(Intercept)' = 'Constant', 'EducSup' = 'Level of Education of the mother: High-SES')
lm1 <- feols(ECSPlanToBaseline~ Educ , data = MainDB, cluster = ~blocksMatWave)

lm2 <- feols(ECSApp~  Educ, data = Control, cluster = ~blocksMatWave)
lm3 <- feols(ECSUseYes~  Educ, data = Control, cluster = ~blocksMatWave)



modelsummary(list(
"Intention" = lm1,    
"Application" = lm2, 
"Access" = lm3

), statistic = "{std.error} ({p.value})",
                      estimate="{estimate}{stars}  [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]",
                      gof_map = c("r.squared" ,"adj.r.squared" ,"nobs", "vcov.type", "FE"="FE: blocksMatWave" ),
                      stars = c("***"=.01,"**"=.05,"*"=.1),
                      title="Probability to be satisfied with the current childcare solution according to education level and ECEC used",
                      notes=list("",
                                 "Coefficient, 95 % CI in brackets, standard errors, p-value or adjusted p-value in parenthesis")
                      ,output = 'flextable',escape=TRUE, coef_map = cm)|>
  autofit()




```

# Regression globale

```{r regression}

library(rio)

db_clean <- dbMachineLearning %>%
  filter(!is.na(ECSPlanToBaseline)) %>%
  mutate(target = as.numeric(ECSPlanToBaseline)) 



# Preparation
## Split the sample
library(tidymodels)
tidymodels_prefer()
set.seed(10)
split <- initial_split(db_clean, prop = 0.8)
train <- training(split)
test <- testing(split)

# Apply the recipe (simplified)
model_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train) %>%
  step_unknown(#Primipare,
               #FmlyIncomeBaseline,
                # IncomeBaseline, 
               TrustCreche, 
               DeprivHolidays,
               #BreastFeedIntend,
               InformalReciprocity, 
             TrustAssMat,
             TrustFam,
             TrustFriend,
             #CoupleCohabiting,
             AccessEasy5, 
             NormsHouse, 
NormsWork, 
LevelInfoSubExPost
) %>%   step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
    step_zv() %>%
   step_impute_knn(all_numeric_predictors(), neighbors = 5) %>%
   # Supprimer les variables à variance nulle
  # Normaliser les prédicteurs numériques
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_YeoJohnson(NormsOpposedN, 
                  AffordCostBaseline
                  #BreastFeedLength,
                  #NumberChildren
                  ) # some variables are skewed. We transform them using YeoJohson that can also deal with missing values

reg_model <-
  linear_reg() %>%
  set_mode("regression") %>%
  set_engine("lm")


# no fit command, because that's part of the recipe

reg_flow <- 
  workflow() %>% # it's a workflow, it's a way of organizing the steps of the model. It's empty. You have to add a model then a receipe
  add_model(reg_model) %>% # we add the model
  add_recipe(model_recipe) # we add the recipe

# Fitting the model to the training data
reg_fit <- fit(reg_flow, train) # fits happy flow to the training data
tidy(reg_fit) # it looks different compared to the previous model, but we imputed the NA and we standardised the coefficients so 
# it's a different metric

# we can also use the model to make predictions on the test set

# Evaluating the model
reg_fit %>%
  predict(test) %>%
  bind_cols(test) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred) # to know how well it performed
# rmse: we aspired to 0 
# rsq: we aspired to 1
# mae: we aspired to 0

## On the full sample

# Fitting the model to the training data
reg_fit <- fit(reg_flow, db_clean) # fits happy flow to the training data
tidy = tidy(reg_fit) %>%  filter(!is.na(estimate)) %>% arrange(desc(estimate))
print(tidy, n = 128)
```

```{r dataset}
# Keep 20% of the observations for the test set.
```

```{r ML}
#| echo: false

# Our recipe. Our task is a classification task because our taget is a categorical variable. 
# step_unkown turns NAs into "unknown" becuse tidymodels and our algo do not like NAs

rf_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train_df)  %>%
  step_unknown(#Primipare,
               #FmlyIncomeBaseline,
                # IncomeBaseline, 
               TrustCreche, 
               DeprivHolidays,
               #BreastFeedIntend,
               InformalReciprocity, 
             TrustAssMat,
             TrustFam,
             TrustFriend,
             #CoupleCohabiting,
             AccessEasy5, 
             NormsHouse, 
NormsWork, 
LevelInfoSubExPost
) %>% 
  # We dummify everything
  step_dummy(#Educ3, 
             #Educ3Dad,
             DiscountRate,
                          AffordSubsidiesBaseline,
             AffordNMCostWBBaseline,
             AffordOppCostBaseline,
             AffordNMCostCareerBaseline,
             AccessHoursBaseline, 
             #BirthPlace3, 
             #FmlyIncomeBaseline,
              #   IncomeBaseline, 
             TrustCreche, 
             LikertReturnHKBaseline, 
             DeprivHolidays, 
             NormsHouse, 
NormsWork, 
LevelInfoSubExPost
             ) %>% 
  step_impute_knn(NormsOpposedN,  # we impute missing values for the numerical variables using knn
                  AffordCostBaseline,
             #     BreastFeedLength,
              #    NumberChildren,
                  neighbors = 5) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson(NormsOpposedN, 
                  AffordCostBaseline
                  #BreastFeedLength,
                  #NumberChildren
                  ) # some variables are skewed. We transform them using YeoJohson that can also deal with missing values

## RUN THE RANDOM FOREST

# In the REAL DEFINITIVE VERSION you should also tune the number of trees, or at least generate 150 of them.
rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), # 100 is a low side. Do at least 150 
                       trees = 10, # if I tune it, it takes forever to run
                       min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>% # IMPORTANT! It can also deal with classes and influence the loss function
  set_engine("partykit")


# Flooow: specify what transformations (recipe) will be done and what algo will be fitted in a first step
initial_flow <- workflow() %>% # create the initial workflow
  add_recipe(rf_recipe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec)


# The argument finalize is key because tidymodels needs to look
# at the data to figure out how many features there are.

# We need to tell tidymodels which parameters need to be tuned. It can conveniently be done with this chunk of code

# In this version we are not tuning the number of trees, but we could.
# We tune mtry and min_n the number of obs in each terminal leaves (you don't want one leaf == 1 obs that's overfitting)
# mtry is the number of features that are randomly selected at each split. It is a good idea to tune it because it can have a big impact on the performance of the model
# Doing this is an argument if I have a lot of predictors/features. At each round, it is only a subsample of predictors that is used. 
rf_para <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_spec) %>% # extract the tuning parameters
  finalize(train_df) # here we have only 2 because we set trees to 100 not tune()
# finalize(train): we need to know the maximum number of features we could fit because it has not looked at the data yet
# it tells tidymodel that he can look at the data quickly to see how many features there are in the data

set.seed(20) # for reproducibility

# Set the tuning grid
# The tuning grid is the set of values of the tuning parameters we seek to evaluate. The larger the better
rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(rf_para,  # we use a latin hypercube here. 
                                size = 50, # 25 random combinations of mtry and min_n LOW! Increase in real life. There are good chances that the "true" combination is not in there
                                variogram_range = 0.75, # explore the space of the hyperparameters
                                original = TRUE)
set.seed(30)

# Set the cross validation. 
# Ideally, we would need to do repetitions of the cross validation to increase the robustness of the results. 
# Do this in the final version with the repeats = 10 argument
# it will create 9 training folds and 1 validation fold. It will do this 10 times.
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_df, v = 10, strata = target) # stratified CV

# Set the metrics used: accuracy or cohen's kappa or F1 for a classification task (or AUC)
rf_metrics <- metric_set(accuracy) # classification task

doParallel::registerDoParallel() # used parallel cores to run the computation

# tune the model, with the cross validation method defined, the grid and the metrics you set
rf_tune <- initial_flow %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds, grid = rf_grid, metrics = rf_metrics)


# select the best parameters for the model the tuning found
rf_best <- select_best(rf_tune)
rf_best# Trees again with X features at each time and X obs at terminal leaves
# 34 features, and 19 obs in terminal leaves

# Update the model with the best parameters found
rf_updated <- finalize_model(rf_spec,
                             rf_best) 

# add this to the initial workflow
workflow_new <- initial_flow %>%
  update_model(rf_updated)

# Fit the model on the training set
rf_fit_final <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = train_df) # fit on the training set

# Fit the model on the test set to evaluate performance
# Performance on the test set
rf_fit_final %>%
  predict(test_df) %>%
  bind_cols(test_df) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred_class)
# the accuracy is great but the kappa not that much (average)
# see if tuning the trees improve this in the future
```

```{r interpretr}

# DALEX want to know a couple of things in the explainer
explainer <- explain_tidymodels( # create the  explainer
  model = rf_fit_final, # what is the model
  data = test_df, # what do you want to explain? The test data? The train data? Something else?
  y = test_df$target # what is the target variable?
)


# SHAPLY VALUES
library(forcats)

set.seed(1995)
shap <- predict_parts(explainer = explainer,
                      new_observation = test_df[, !(names(test_df) %in% "target")], # remove the target
                      type = "shap", 
                      B = 20)

average_shapley <- shap %>% 
  group_by(variable) %>% 
  summarise(contribution = mean(contribution)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(abs(contribution)))


shap %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(mean_val = mean(contribution)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, abs(mean_val))) %>% # reorder the variables according to their contribution in term of their absolute value
  ggplot(aes(contribution, variable, fill = mean_val > 0)) +
  geom_col(data = ~distinct(., variable, mean_val), 
           aes(mean_val, variable), 
           alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
s <- skim(work_df)
print(s, include_summary = FALSE)
# We have NA for ECSIdealAgeEntryBaseline, TrustCreche, BreastFeedLength, NormsOpposedN, AffordCostBaseline, NumberChildren we may want to impute them


# Keep 20% of the observations for the test set.
set.seed(1451)
credit_split <- initial_split(work_df, prop = 0.8)
train_df <- training(credit_split)
test_df <- testing(credit_split)


## MACHINE LEARNING


rf_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = train_df)  %>%
  step_unknown(#Primipare,
               #FmlyIncomeBaseline,
                # IncomeBaseline, 
               TrustCreche, 
               DeprivHolidays,
               #BreastFeedIntend,
               InformalReciprocity, 
             TrustAssMat,
             TrustFam,
             TrustFriend,
             #CoupleCohabiting,
             AccessEasy5, 
             NormsHouse, 
NormsWork, 
LevelInfoSubExPost
) %>% 
  # We dummify everything
  step_dummy(#Educ3, 
             #Educ3Dad,
             DiscountRate,
                          AffordSubsidiesBaseline,
             AffordNMCostWBBaseline,
             AffordOppCostBaseline,
             AffordNMCostCareerBaseline,
             AccessHoursBaseline, 
             #BirthPlace3, 
             #FmlyIncomeBaseline,
              #   IncomeBaseline, 
             TrustCreche, 
             LikertReturnHKBaseline, 
             DeprivHolidays, 
             NormsHouse, 
NormsWork, 
LevelInfoSubExPost, 
Assignment
             ) %>% 
  step_impute_knn(NormsOpposedN,  # we impute missing values for the numerical variables using knn
                  AffordCostBaseline,
             #     BreastFeedLength,
              #    NumberChildren,
                  neighbors = 5) %>% 
  step_YeoJohnson(NormsOpposedN, 
                  AffordCostBaseline
                  #BreastFeedLength,
                  #NumberChildren
                  ) # some variables are skewed. We transform them using YeoJohson that can also deal with missing values

## RUN THE RANDOM FOREST

# In the REAL DEFINITIVE VERSION you should also tune the number of trees, or at least generate 150 of them.
rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), # 100 is a low side. Do at least 150 
                       trees = 10, # if I tune it, it takes forever to run
                       min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>% # IMPORTANT! It can also deal with classes and influence the loss function
  set_engine("partykit")


# Flooow: specify what transformations (recipe) will be done and what algo will be fitted in a first step
initial_flow <- workflow() %>% # create the initial workflow
  add_recipe(rf_recipe) %>%
  add_model(rf_spec)


# The argument finalize is key because tidymodels needs to look
# at the data to figure out how many features there are.

# We need to tell tidymodels which parameters need to be tuned. It can conveniently be done with this chunk of code

# In this version we are not tuning the number of trees, but we could.
# We tune mtry and min_n the number of obs in each terminal leaves (you don't want one leaf == 1 obs that's overfitting)
# mtry is the number of features that are randomly selected at each split. It is a good idea to tune it because it can have a big impact on the performance of the model
# Doing this is an argument if I have a lot of predictors/features. At each round, it is only a subsample of predictors that is used. 
rf_para <- extract_parameter_set_dials(rf_spec) %>% # extract the tuning parameters
  finalize(train_df) # here we have only 2 because we set trees to 100 not tune()
# finalize(train): we need to know the maximum number of features we could fit because it has not looked at the data yet
# it tells tidymodel that he can look at the data quickly to see how many features there are in the data

set.seed(20) # for reproducibility

# Set the tuning grid
# The tuning grid is the set of values of the tuning parameters we seek to evaluate. The larger the better
rf_grid <- grid_latin_hypercube(rf_para,  # we use a latin hypercube here. 
                                size = 50, # 25 random combinations of mtry and min_n LOW! Increase in real life. There are good chances that the "true" combination is not in there
                                variogram_range = 0.75, # explore the space of the hyperparameters
                                original = TRUE)
set.seed(30)

# Set the cross validation. 
# Ideally, we would need to do repetitions of the cross validation to increase the robustness of the results. 
# Do this in the final version with the repeats = 10 argument
# it will create 9 training folds and 1 validation fold. It will do this 10 times.
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(train_df, v = 10, strata = target) # stratified CV

# Set the metrics used: accuracy or cohen's kappa or F1 for a classification task (or AUC)
rf_metrics <- metric_set(accuracy) # classification task

doParallel::registerDoParallel() # used parallel cores to run the computation

# tune the model, with the cross validation method defined, the grid and the metrics you set
rf_tune <- initial_flow %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds, grid = rf_grid, metrics = rf_metrics)


# select the best parameters for the model the tuning found
rf_best <- select_best(rf_tune)
rf_best# Trees again with X features at each time and X obs at terminal leaves
# 34 features, and 19 obs in terminal leaves

# Update the model with the best parameters found
rf_updated <- finalize_model(rf_spec,
                             rf_best) 

# add this to the initial workflow
workflow_new <- initial_flow %>%
  update_model(rf_updated)

# Fit the model on the training set
rf_fit_final <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = train_df) # fit on the training set

# Fit the model on the test set to evaluate performance
# Performance on the test set
rf_fit_final %>%
  predict(test_df) %>%
  bind_cols(test_df) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred_class)
# the accuracy is great but the kappa not that much (average)
# see if tuning the trees improve this in the future
```

```{r}
library(rio)

lasso_clean <- MainDB %>%
  filter(!is.na(ECSPlanToBaseline)) %>%
  mutate(target = as.numeric(ECSPlanToBaseline)) %>% # specify the target
  select(c(target, # we select the variables that we want. Check that there are the same than below. Obsiouvly, there are several variables that were recoded, and we don't want to have both the recoded version and the original one as they are colinear. 
           NormsOpposedN,
           AffordCostBaseline, 
           #Educ3, # on laisse educ et educ dad mais je suis pas sûre que ce soit pertinent. Idem pour les variables de revenu
             #Educ3Dad, 
           DiscountRate,
     ComputerYN,
     AffordSubsidiesBaseline,
             AffordNMCostWBBaseline,
             AffordOppCostBaseline,
             AffordNMCostCareerBaseline,
             DiscountRate,
             AccessHoursBaseline, 
   #  Primipare, #to check 
    # BirthPlace3, 
    # Active,  
AccessInformalFullTime,
#Age,
#SingleMum, 
#FmlyIncomeBaseline,
 #               IncomeBaseline,
                LikertReturnHKBaseline,
                TrustCreche,
TrustAssMat,
                KnowsCreche,
                KnowsAssMat, 
     ComputerYN ,
     HighLowECECBaseline ,
            #     BreastFeedIntend,
            #     BreastFeedLength, 
Language3,
                InformalReciprocity, # Do the parents already take care of the children of others
                AffordCostDK, 
                AffordCostBaseline,
             #    AccessEasyBaseline,
                 NormsBaseline,
                LikertAccessInfoBaseline, # strongly disagree, disagree, don't know, agree, strongly agree
                LikertAccessSoc, # strongly disagree, disagree, don't know, agree, strongly agree
                 DeprivClothes, # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to buy clothes?
                DeprivFood, # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to buy food?
                DeprivBills, # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to pay for the bills?
                DeprivHolidays, # DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to go in holidays?
                DeprivHousing,# DEPRIVATION: do parents struggle to pay for housing?              
#NumberChildren,
                TrustFam,
                TrustFriend,
#   CoupleCohabiting,
AccessEasy5, 
NormsHouse, 
NormsWork, 
LevelInfoSubExPost
)) %>%      mutate(across(where(is.logical), as.numeric)) 




# Preparation
## Split the sample
library(tidymodels)
tidymodels_prefer()
set.seed(10)
lasso_split <- initial_split(lasso_clean, prop = 0.8)
lasso_train <- training(lasso_split)
lasso_test <- testing(lasso_split)

# Apply the recipe (simplified)
model_recipe <- recipe(target ~ ., data = lasso_train) %>%
  step_unknown(#Primipare,
               #FmlyIncomeBaseline,
                # IncomeBaseline, 
               TrustCreche, 
               DeprivHolidays,
               #BreastFeedIntend,
               InformalReciprocity, 
             TrustAssMat,
             TrustFam,
             TrustFriend,
             #CoupleCohabiting,
             AccessEasy5, 
             NormsHouse, 
NormsWork, 
LevelInfoSubExPost
) %>%   step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE) %>%
    step_zv() %>%
   step_impute_knn(all_numeric_predictors(), neighbors = 5) %>%
   # Supprimer les variables à variance nulle
  # Normaliser les prédicteurs numériques
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_YeoJohnson(NormsOpposedN, 
                  AffordCostBaseline
                  #BreastFeedLength,
                  #NumberChildren
                  ) # some variables are skewed. We transform them using YeoJohson that can also deal with missing values

# Model specification
lasso_spec <-  linear_reg(penalty = tune(), # here we need something new
                          mixture = 1) %>% # penalty is the lambda parameter
  # mixture is the alpha. Alpha = 1 is just the lasso
  # Penalty is tune ()
  set_mode("regression") %>% # we are still doing regression
  set_engine("glmnet") # we use a different engine that does regularisation

lasso_wf <- workflow() %>% # define the workflow
  add_model(lasso_spec) %>%
  add_recipe(model_recipe)

elastic_metrics <- metric_set(rsq) # we select metrics, we don't want the 3
# we use the rsq metric

# Resampling methods: 10 fold cross-validation
set.seed(20)
cv_folds <- vfold_cv(lasso_train,
                     v = 10,
                     repeats = 5)

# Using dials to tune the model: 
glmnet_param <- extract_parameter_set_dials(lasso_spec)# it extracts for me the parameter that 
# needs to be tuned
glmnet_param

# Set the grid
set.seed(15)
lasso_grid <- grid_max_entropy(glmnet_param,
                               size = 50, # generate 50 different lambdas
                               # 50 is a bit low, 100 or 150 is better
                               original = TRUE, # we are keeoing the original scale, the log
                               variogram_range = 0.5) # the higher the value, the less likely it is to explore 

# Vérifier que la recette fonctionne
prep(model_recipe) %>%
  bake(new_data = NULL) %>%
  glimpse()

# Tuning the Hyper-Parameter
doParallel::registerDoParallel() # to know how many cores to use at the same time
lasso_tune <- lasso_wf %>%
  tune_grid(cv_folds,
            grid = lasso_grid, # use the grid we just created
            metrics = elastic_metrics)
# So far we've selected 50 values of lambda. It run a regression for each lambda within each fold
# We are running 50 * 10 * 5 = 2500 regressions in total, which all has a different R2

# Plot the (average) performance
autoplot(lasso_tune) # x is different values of lambda in the log scale. y is the average R2

# Select the best lambda
lasso_best <- select_best(lasso_tune)
lasso_best # Model 46 

temp <- collect_metrics(lasso_tune)
print(temp, n = 50) # print all the 50 lambdas
# the std error is the variance divided by the square root of N
# We see that model 46 is the best, but we can also see that the difference between the best and the worst is not that big

# Finalizing the fit
lasso_updated <- finalize_model(lasso_spec, # I finalize by using the pre specified moded
                                lasso_best) # this replace the spec() argument by the picked lambda
workflow_new <- lasso_wf %>%
  update_model(lasso_updated)

new_fit <- workflow_new %>%
  fit(data = lasso_train)

tidy_lasso <- new_fit %>%
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>%
  tidy()

tidy_lasso # generosity got kicked out

# Evaluating the model: performance
new_fit %>%
  predict(lasso_test) %>%
  bind_cols(lasso_test) %>%
  metrics(truth = target, estimate = .pred)

```

```{r}
## POST LASSO 

lasso_var <- tidy_lasso %>% 
  filter(estimate != 0) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  pull(term)  # Liste des variables sélectionnées

# Appliquer la recipe sur les données d'entraînement
lasso_train_baked <- prep(model_recipe_post) %>% # we preprosess the data
  bake(new_data = lasso_train) # it creates the dataset normalized and transformed

# We do the same for the test set 
lasso_test_baked <- prep(model_recipe_post) %>% # should we apply the transformatios ? 
  bake(new_data = lasso_test)

# Select only the variables that the lasso picked up
lasso_train_post <- lasso_train_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var))) # we select the target and the variables that the lasso picked up

lasso_test_post <- lasso_test_baked %>%
  select(all_of(c("target", lasso_var)))

# Fit the model on the training set 
post_lasso_model <- lm(target ~ ., data = lasso_train_post)


# Accuracy on the test set
post_lasso_preds <- predict(post_lasso_model, newdata = lasso_test_post)

# Calculer les métriques
post_lasso_metrics <- metrics(
  data = data.frame(truth = lasso_test_post$target, estimate = post_lasso_preds),
  truth = truth,
  estimate = estimate
)
print(post_lasso_metrics)
```
